subject: EOS Health: request for evidence on selective debug-trace preservation
messages:
From: Eli Chen <eli.chen@eoshealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: EOS Health Legal <legal@eoshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Selective debug-trace retention — evidence request

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our SIG/CAIQ follow-up, our security team needs an evidence package showing how Redwood handles selective retention of debug traces for tenant-scoped incidents. Specifically we need:

- A description of the mechanism that pins a small set of debug traces to a customer retention window beyond the standard TTL
- Where those traces live (KEKs/KMS, storage tier) and how they are isolated from normal telemetry
- A signed or time-stamped proof that traces marked for a legal hold can be retained for up to 540 days with controlled access
- Any compensating controls you rely on if retention is extended (access logs, role separation, encryption in transit+at rest)

Can you provide the artifacts and a short one-page narrative that our SOC reviewer can attach to the SIG? We prefer a ZIP (namespaced) and a simple CSV mapping trace types -> retention policy.

–Eli
Eli Chen
Security Operations
EOS Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Selective debug-trace retention — evidence request

Neha / Karthik — forwarding the EOS ask. They want an evidence ZIP + CSV mapping. From previous discussions this looks like a hybrid of the ephemeral session carveouts and a tenant-scoped legal hold path.

Quick thoughts / asks:
- Neha: can you pull the retention matrix for tenant-scoped debug traces and confirm which storage buckets + KMS keys are used when we apply a targeted hold?
- Karthik: can your team produce the one-page narrative (operational steps + access controls) and a short export of the access logs for April 2026 (redact internal IPs) to demonstrate auditability?

I don’t want to promise the 540d outright in the customer-facing doc without confirmation from infra on cost/viability, but we should be explicit about compensating controls if we can’t commit to that window.

I’ll coordinate attachments and hit reply-all to Eli once we have drafts.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Selective debug-trace retention — evidence request

On Fri, Apr 3, 2026 at 10:04 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Neha / Karthik — forwarding the EOS ask. They want an evidence ZIP + CSV mapping. From previous discussions this looks like a hybrid of the ephemeral session carveouts and a tenant-scoped legal hold path.

Following up with the infra runbook owners:
- Mechanism: when a tenant-scoped debug trace is flagged for extended retention, we create a namespaced object in the "customer-hold" bucket under the same region as the tenant. That object is encrypted with a customer-scoped KMS key (CMK) that is rotated according to our KMS policy.
- Storage: held traces are kept in a separate S3 path with access via an internal RBAC-only role (no public access). Lifecycle rules are disabled for objects in the customer-hold prefix; these objects are excluded from background TTL pruning.
- Proof: attached a csv (keystore-retention-matrix.csv) that maps trace category -> bucket prefix -> KMS key alias -> maximum allowed hold days (operationally set to 540 for legal holds; product-level defaults differ).
- Controls: we maintain per-object access logs (CloudTrail + internal audit pipeline), HSM-backed key material for CMKs, MFA enforced for any key destruction operations, and quarterly separation-of-duty review.

I also attached a small sample export of the access audit for the sample object we used in the demo. I redacted IPs and removed unrelated tenant ids.

Attachments included in my reply: evidence-pack-v1.zip (manifest + narrative), keystore-retention-matrix.csv, sample-access-audit.csv

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Infra Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Eli Chen <eli.chen@eoshealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: EOS Health Legal <legal@eoshealth.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Selective debug-trace retention — evidence request

Monica / Neha — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifying asks from our reviewer: 

1) In the CSV matrix the KMS key aliases reference a customer-scoped CMK; can you confirm that EOS Health’s tenant uses a dedicated alias (not a shared alias) and provide the alias string we can reference in the SIG attachments?
2) For the access logs included in evidence-pack-v1.zip, can you add an explicit line showing an RBAC deny event to prove separation of duties? (we need an example deny and the remediation ticket id).
3) Given this path, does Redwood have a documented operational SLA for restoring held traces for eDiscovery requests? If so, please include the runbook link and the average RTO observed in the last 12 months.

If you can update the ZIP with those three items, we can include it in our SIG submission and close this control. Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

Best,
Eli
